claim: Jev has a single evaluation endpoint, POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, selected per call by the request's model field; GET /v1/models lists names.
quote: Every model on this page is served by the same endpoint, `POST /v1/systemone`. The request's `model` field selects which one handles the call; see the API reference for the full request shape.

claim: A live probe on 2026-10-02 of api.typesafe.ai/v1/models without a key returned HTTP 403 authentication_error 'Must supply an API key!' served via Cloudflare; the bare host root returns 404.
quote: {"detail":{"error_type":"authentication_error","message":"Must supply an API key! Check your request and try again."}}
why: Confirms the official host is live and key-gated; matches the 403 row in third-party error tables.

claim: The API reference caps a Choice at 255 options and a Score at 2 to 10 levels, and documents 422 (validation), 429 (rate limit) and 529 (overloaded) errors.
quote: You can have a maximum of 255 options per Choice. ... An ordered array of level descriptions. A Score should have at least two levels; the API accepts up to 10.
why: Question types (choice/score/noul) and their limits, plus error codes a client must handle.

claim: Official docs list jev-1.13.0 limits as 64k tokens per request (32k for state plus longest question) and 100K tokens/s / 40 requests/s, adjusting dynamically without notice.
quote: Rate limits | 100K tokens per second / 40 requests per second | Context length | 64k tokens per request; 32k tokens for `state` plus the longest question ... the limits above can change without notice
why: Context and rate limits; note conflict with the 1,200 rpm / 250k tok/s figure on third-party pages (Q1-05).

claim: Third-party guides report Jev rate limits of 1,200 requests/minute and 250,000 tokens/second, which conflicts with the current official 40 req/s / 100K tok/s.
quote: Rate limits: 1,200 requests per minute and 250,000 tokens per second, adjusted dynamically by TypeSafe. We saw no rate-limit headers on responses.
why: Rate-limit conflict: probably an earlier docs version; shows limits have moved since launch.

claim: Jev list price is $0.042 per million input tokens ($42 per billion); output tokens are free, and TypeSafe says it cannot prove the price is not subsidized.
quote: Input tokens: $0.042 / MTok ($ 42 per billion tokens). Output tokens: FREE (too cheap to meter).
why: Pricing per token; the same blog notes 'We can't prove it isn't subsidized', relevant to price stability.

claim: As of 2026-10-02 TypeSafe's own homepage still presents Jev as early access with a 'Join Waitlist' call to action; the launch post says developers are brought off the waitlist progressively.
quote: Today, we are opening early access and bringing developers off the waitlist as quickly as we can.
why: Access status. Homepage text fetched 2026-10-02 includes 'Join Waitlist' and 'Try our first System One Model, Jev, in early access.'

claim: A model directory claims Jev became generally available with no waitlist on 2026-09-20 via console.typesafe.ai, contradicting the official site's waitlist wording.
quote: generally available to everyone with no waitlist as of 2026-09-20 via https://console.typesafe.ai/
why: Access-status conflict; unsourced aggregator claim, needs confirmation from TypeSafe itself.

claim: jev-latest and jev-preview are both aliases pointing to jev-1.13.0; aliases move on release and TypeSafe advises pinning the versioned ID when confidence thresholds are tuned.
quote: If you have tuned confidence thresholds against a specific version, pin that version's ID instead of the alias and move to the new one on your own schedule.
why: Versioning/pinning; directly relevant to a gatherer that thresholds Jev scores.

claim: An independent test on 2026-09-19 found 'jev-1.13' rejected with HTTP 400 Unknown model, and a ~33,600-token request rejected with max_tokens_exceeded while 32,204 tokens passed.
quote: `jev-1.13` | HTTP 400, “Unknown model: jev-1.13”, even though one example in TypeSafe’s own docs uses this spelling
why: Pinning gotcha (must use full jev-1.13.0) and the effective 32k state ceiling in practice.

claim: Cloudflare Workers AI lists TypeSafe's Jev as model typesafe/jev with a 32,000-token context window and pricing only in the Cloudflare dashboard.
quote: Jev is TypeSafe's structured evaluation model. It evaluates one state against typed Noul, Choice, and Score questions ... Context Window | 32,000 tokens ... Pricing | View pricing in the Cloudflare dashboard
why: Official secondary host; smaller context than TypeSafe direct (32k vs 64k), example response reports jev-1.13.0.

claim: jevtypesafeai.com is run by CODEFASHION TECH LTD, is not affiliated with TypeSafe AI, forwards state and questions upstream via its own /api/v1/decide with jv_live_ keys, and lists $0.25-$0.42/M input.
quote: jevtypesafeai.com is an independent developer platform . It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by TypeSafe AI ... The Service is operated by CODEFASHION TECH LTD . ... We forward the request state and typed questions
why: Answers who runs the look-alike domain; a reseller/proxy at up to 10x list price that sees all request text (also relevant to Q5).

claim: Other third-party routes exist: OpenRouter lists typesafe/jev-1.13 at $0.042/M via an alpha decisions endpoint, Vercel AI Gateway as typesafe-ai/jev, and apimodels.app resells at $0.05/M.
quote: POST`https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions` ... Model`typesafe/jev-1.13` ... Jev 1.13 costs $0.042/M input tokens and $0.00/M output tokens.
why: Map of non-TypeSafe hosts and their model IDs; OpenRouter endpoint is alpha and uses a different model slug.

claim: Official SDKs are PyPI typesafe-sdk 0.7.2 (author TypeSafe AI, Python >=3.10) and npm @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 (maintainers @typesafe.ai); the Rust typesafe-jev crate and Ruby typesafe-jev gem are third-party.
why: SDK inventory. Registry checks 2026-10-02: npm maintainers allie@/diogo@typesafe.ai; crates.io typesafe-jev repo github.com/thehumanworks/jevgrep; rubygems typesafe-jev owner dtheo (github dtheofr).
